newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom welcomes government mission.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom welcomes government mission.

text.p: France Telecom on Friday welcomed a decision by Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to name an envoy to lead consultations with staff and management at the telecoms operator which had been slated for partial privatisation.
"We welcome the nomination of Michel Delebarre and France Telecom, chairman Michel Bon in particular, are at his disposition," a company spokesman said.
Delebarre has to report back to the government on September 5.
"The new government said it needed time to think things over. This appointment means that that things are moving," the spokesman added.
France Telecom chairman Bon is in favour of a partial privatisation of the company so that it can be better armed to face the competition in a liberalised French and European market from 1998.
"The decision is up to the government. The position of France Telecom is well known," the spokesman said.
The previous conservative government had been planning to bring some 35 percent of France Telecom to the market in the country's biggest ever International Public Offering (IPO).

The operation, initially scheduled for May, was postponed by a month after President Jacques Chirac called an early parliamentary election and suspended after the Socialist party formed a government with the communists and greens.
The Communist party is opposed to any privatisation. Jospin had during his campaign promised that he would "consult" the France Telecom staff before taking a decision on the future of the company.
Since taking office, the Socialists have said that there could be sales of minority stakes in state companies which operate in a competitive market.
The France Telecom spokesman said reports in a French newspaper that the operators' first half results were below expectations of the banks preparing its IPO were "rubbish".
"Our first half results are not yet known. They will be published on September 17," he said.
